evals.query: I have a UserService proto with a GetUser RPC. In my Kora service, how do I call it from a component?
expected_behavior: Enables io.koraframework.grpc.client.GrpcClientModule on the @KoraApp interface
Injects UserServiceGrpc.UserServiceBlockingStub directly by type via constructor with no @Tag on the parameter
Annotates the wrapper with @Component imported from io.koraframework.common.annotation
Builds the request with GetUserRequest.newBuilder() and calls stub.getUser(request) synchronously
Adds implementation "io.koraframework:grpc-client" plus the annotation processor (Java) or KSP (Kotlin)
Keeps protobuf types and StatusRuntimeException handling inside the wrapper component
anti_behavior: Imports ru.tinkoff.grpc.client.GrpcClientModule or ru.tinkoff.kora.common.Component
Puts @Tag on the stub constructor parameter
Returns Mono, Flux, CompletionStage or declares the method suspend
Uses field injection or a foreign-framework annotation

evals.query: Our Kora 1.x service depends on ru.tinkoff.kora:grpc-client and its @KoraApp extends ru.tinkoff.grpc.client.GrpcClientModule. What are the Kora 2.0 equivalents?
expected_behavior: States the artifact is io.koraframework:grpc-client
States the module interface is io.koraframework.grpc.client.GrpcClientModule
Mentions the BOM change ru.tinkoff.kora:kora-parent -> io.koraframework:kora-bom at 2.0.0.RC2 from mavenCentral()
States that DI annotations moved to io.koraframework.common.annotation
Confirms what did NOT change: stubs still inject by type untagged, interceptors are still scoped with @Tag(<Service>Grpc.class), the config section is still grpcClient.<protoServiceName>
anti_behavior: Claims io.koraframework:grpc-client-module or any artifact name other than grpc-client
Recommends 2.0.0-SNAPSHOT or 2.0.0.alpha6 as the version for a new project
Suggests a blind package find/replace as the whole migration
Claims the gRPC client API is unchanged because the migration guides do not discuss it

evals.query: Configure my Kora gRPC client for UserService with a 10 second timeout and metrics enabled, reading the server URL from an environment variable.
expected_behavior: Places the config under grpcClient.UserService, using the proto service simple name
Sets the required url key and overrides it with ${?GRPC_SERVER_URL}
Sets timeout = "10s" and telemetry.metrics.enabled = true explicitly
States that telemetry.metrics.enabled and telemetry.logging.enabled default to false in Kora 2.0 (tracing defaults to true)
Notes that metrics also require a MeterRegistry in the graph (io.koraframework:micrometer-module)
Uses an http:// URL for plaintext rather than a usePlaintext flag
anti_behavior: Writes maxInboundMessageSize, usePlaintext, or a retry key under grpcClient
Claims metrics are enabled by default
Names the section grpcClient.UserServiceGrpc or after java_outer_classname
Invents config keys not present in GrpcClientConfig

evals.query: I ported this from Kora 1.x and it does nothing: grpcClient { UserService { url = "grpc://users:8090", maxInboundMessageSize = 16777216 } }. Why?
expected_behavior: Identifies that maxInboundMessageSize is not a key in Kora 2.0 GrpcClientConfig and is silently ignored — config-common performs no unknown-key validation
Points at a tagged Configurer<ManagedChannelBuilder<?>> component as the 2.0 way to set maxInboundMessageSize
Identifies grpc:// as the second bug: usePlaintext() is called only for the http scheme, so this URL silently uses TLS
Rewrites the URL to http://users:8090
Lists the real key set: url, timeout, keepAliveTime, keepAliveTimeout, loadBalancingPolicy, defaultServiceConfig, telemetry.*
anti_behavior: Claims an unknown config key produces an error or warning at startup
Keeps grpc:// as a valid plaintext scheme
Suggests a usePlaintext config key
Says maxInboundMessageSize just needs a different value or format

evals.query: My Kora 2.0 gRPC client fails with a TLS handshake error against a plaintext local server. The config says url = "grpc://localhost:8090". What is wrong?
expected_behavior: Explains that ManagedChannelLifecycle calls usePlaintext() only when the URL scheme is exactly http
Explains that a non-http scheme WITH an explicit port is accepted and silently uses TLS, which is why there is no config error
Notes that a non-http/https scheme WITHOUT a port throws IllegalArgumentException: Unsupported gRPC client URL scheme
Changes the URL to http://localhost:8090
Mentions that https:// plus a tagged ChannelCredentials component is the path for real TLS
anti_behavior: Suggests adding a usePlaintext or plaintext config key
Claims grpc:// is the canonical Kora scheme
Recommends disabling TLS verification

evals.query: Set up the Gradle build for a Java Kora 2.0 gRPC client, including protobuf code generation.
expected_behavior: Applies the com.google.protobuf Gradle plugin at 0.10.0 and configures protoc plus protoc-gen-grpc-java
Pins the BOM with platform("io.koraframework:kora-bom:$koraVersion") where koraVersion=2.0.0.RC2, without versioning individual io.koraframework artifacts
Adds annotationProcessor "io.koraframework:annotation-processors"
Declares io.koraframework:grpc-client and io.grpc:grpc-protobuf:1.84.0
Pins protoc to 3.25.3 and protoc-gen-grpc-java to 1.84.0
Leaves protobuf-java to resolve transitively from grpc-protobuf (3.25.9) rather than pinning it
Adds compileOnly javax.annotation:javax.annotation-api for javax.annotation.Generated in the generated stubs
Adds build/generated/source/proto/main/{grpc,java} to sourceSets.main.java
Sets the Java toolchain to 25
anti_behavior: Uses ru.tinkoff.kora:kora-parent or ru.tinkoff.kora:annotation-processors
Pins io.grpc artifacts to 1.74.0 or any version other than 1.84.0
Bumps protoc to 4.36.2 WITHOUT also declaring com.google.protobuf:protobuf-java:4.36.2
Assumes kora-bom manages gRPC or protobuf versions
Sets the toolchain below Java 25

evals.query: Set up build.gradle.kts for a Kotlin Kora 2.0 gRPC client with protobuf generation.
expected_behavior: Applies org.jetbrains.kotlin.jvm 2.4.20, com.google.devtools.ksp 2.3.12 and com.google.protobuf 0.10.0
Adds ksp("io.koraframework:symbol-processors:...") and the kora-bom platform at 2.0.0.RC2
Registers the generated proto dirs on sourceSets.main.java, not on kotlin.srcDir, because protoc-gen-grpc-java emits Java
Pins protoc 3.25.3, protoc-gen-grpc-java 1.84.0 and io.grpc:grpc-protobuf 1.84.0
Leaves protobuf-java transitive rather than pinning it
Sets the jvmToolchain to 25
Points mainClass at <package>.ApplicationKt
anti_behavior: Puts the generated gRPC sources on kotlin.srcDir only
Uses ru.tinkoff.kora:symbol-processors
Bumps protoc to 4.36.2 without also pinning protobuf-java:4.36.2
Adds grpc-kotlin-stub without being asked and presents coroutine stubs as the Kora default
Pins Kotlin or KSP to versions inconsistent with 2.4.20 / 2.3.12

evals.query: My Kora 2.0 gRPC client tests fail at runtime with java.lang.AbstractMethodError: ... does not define or inherit an implementation of the resolved method 'buildClientTransportServers(List, MetricRecorder)'. The build compiles fine.
expected_behavior: Identifies this as a gRPC version mismatch, not a Kora bug
Explains that the test transport (io.grpc:grpc-inprocess or grpc-netty) is pinned to a different version than the grpc-core arriving with io.koraframework:grpc-client
Says kora-bom constrains io.koraframework artifacts only, so gRPC versions are the application's responsibility
Aligns every io.grpc artifact on 1.84.0 across main and test source sets
Optionally suggests a resolutionStrategy.eachDependency rule to make the alignment enforceable
anti_behavior: Blames the Kora annotation processor or suggests regenerating the graph
Suggests excluding grpc-core or downgrading Kora
Cites KORA_2_FRAMEWORK_ISSUES.md or KORA_2_MIGRATION_STATUS.md
Recommends adding grpc-inprocess without pinning its version

evals.query: Add an authorization metadata header to every outbound gRPC call to UserService, reading the token from a config component.
expected_behavior: Implements io.grpc.ClientInterceptor as a @Component from io.koraframework.common.annotation
Scopes the interceptor with @Tag(UserServiceGrpc.class) using io.koraframework.common.annotation.Tag
Wraps the call in ForwardingClientCall.SimpleForwardingClientCall and puts the header inside start() before super.start()
Uses Metadata.Key.of("authorization", Metadata.ASCII_STRING_MARSHALLER)
Injects the credential through the constructor, e.g. from an @ConfigSource interface in io.koraframework.config.common.annotation
States that gRPC metadata is the only client auth mechanism — there is no Kora gRPC client auth module
anti_behavior: Imports ru.tinkoff.kora.common.Tag or ru.tinkoff.kora.common.Component
Writes headers outside start(), or after calling super.start()
Invents a Kora gRPC auth annotation or an auth config key under grpcClient
Uses field injection for the config

evals.query: My Kora 2.0 client interceptor is a @Component but it never runs — no log lines, and calls come back UNAUTHENTICATED. It is annotated @Tag(GrpcClientModule.class). Everything compiles and the app starts fine.
expected_behavior: Identifies the tag as the bug: ManagedChannelLifecycle requests All<ClientInterceptor> under @Tag(<Service>Grpc.class), the protoc-generated outer class
Replaces it with @Tag(UserServiceGrpc.class) or the matching generated class
Explains that a wrong or missing tag compiles and starts cleanly, so the failure is silent
Notes that the stub class and Kora module classes are both wrong tag choices
Recommends a test that asserts the header actually arrives, since nothing at startup reports the mistake
anti_behavior: Suggests removing the @Tag entirely as the fix
Suggests tagging the stub constructor parameter instead
Claims Kora logs a warning for an uncollected interceptor
Recommends registering the interceptor by calling ManagedChannelBuilder.intercept manually in application code

evals.query: Our Kora 2.0 gRPC client produces no rpc.client.call.duration metric and no request logs, although the service is definitely making calls. Config only sets grpcClient.UserService.url.
expected_behavior: States that telemetry.logging.enabled and telemetry.metrics.enabled default to false in Kora 2.0
Enables them explicitly under grpcClient.UserService.telemetry
Notes metrics additionally need a MeterRegistry in the graph and tracing needs a Tracer, since the telemetry factory checks both the flag and the component
Mentions the two loggers are named <fullProtoServiceName>.request and .response, so logging.levels must also allow INFO
Notes tracing.enabled defaults to true
anti_behavior: Claims metrics or logging are on by default
Suggests a global telemetry switch outside the grpcClient section as the fix
Invents a metric name other than rpc.client.call.duration (rpc.client.duration is the pre-RC2 name)
Says the logger is named after the Java stub class

evals.query: Port this Kora 1.x gRPC client helper to 2.0: `public UserResponse getUser(Context ctx, String id)` — it took ru.tinkoff.kora.common.Context and propagated it into the call.
expected_behavior: States that Context was removed from the entire Kora framework in 2.0 — there is no io.koraframework equivalent
Removes the Context parameter and passes the needed values as ordinary method parameters
Distinguishes io.grpc.Context as a different, unrelated class that gRPC still ships and that a ClientInterceptor may legitimately use
Notes that contracts are synchronous on virtual threads, so there is no async boundary requiring an ambient carrier
Puts any cross-cutting metadata propagation into a tagged ClientInterceptor instead
anti_behavior: Imports io.koraframework.common.Context or claims Kora Context still exists under a new package
Confuses io.grpc.Context with the removed Kora Context
Reintroduces a ThreadLocal-based Kora-style context as the recommended pattern
Makes the method suspend or return a CompletionStage to carry the context

evals.query: In our Kotlin Kora 2.0 service, can I inject a grpc-kotlin coroutine stub and call its suspend methods from a @Component? What do the Kora examples do?
expected_behavior: States that the KSP extension does resolve io.grpc.kotlin.AbstractCoroutineStub subclasses annotated @StubFor, so injection is supported
Clarifies that a generated suspend fun on such a stub is grpc-kotlin's code, not a Kora contract — Kora provides no coroutine scope to call it from
States that Kora 2.0 contracts are synchronous on virtual threads
Says no migrated Kora example uses coroutine stubs; both Kotlin examples use the Java *BlockingStub / *Stub with StreamObserver
Recommends the Java stubs, and notes grpc-kotlin 1.5.0 plus protoc-gen-grpc-kotlin must be added and kept aligned with grpc-java 1.84.0 if coroutine stubs are used anyway
anti_behavior: Claims Kora 2.0 supports suspend gRPC client contracts
Claims coroutine stubs were removed from Kora 2.0 and cannot be injected
Recommends runBlocking or Dispatchers.IO as the way to bridge Kora to a coroutine stub without noting it is the caller's own boundary
Presents coroutine stubs as the Kotlin default for Kora

evals.query: Consume a server-streaming GetAllUsers RPC and collect all results into a list in my Kora 2.0 client.
expected_behavior: Injects UserServiceGrpc.UserServiceBlockingStub and drains the returned Iterator, e.g. with forEachRemaining
Or uses the async UserServiceGrpc.UserServiceStub with a StreamObserver implementing onNext/onError/onCompleted
Keeps stream handling inside a @Component wrapper and maps protobuf messages to application DTOs there
Notes that a per-client timeout applies to the whole call, so a long stream needs it unset or overridden per call
Notes the iterator must be drained or the call cancelled, otherwise the stream stays open
anti_behavior: Returns Flux, Flow or a suspend function as the Kora contract
Uses runBlocking or Dispatchers.IO to bridge the stream in Kotlin
Leaks StreamObserver callbacks into a controller
Claims Kora provides a reactive gRPC client contract

evals.query: Implement a client-streaming CreateUsers call that pushes multiple requests and awaits one summary response.
expected_behavior: Injects the async UserServiceGrpc.UserServiceStub
Obtains the request StreamObserver from asyncStub.createUsers(responseObserver)
Calls requestObserver.onNext(...) per request and requestObserver.onCompleted() at the end
Bridges the async result to the synchronous contract with a CompletableFuture completed inside the response observer, using a timed get
Calls requestObserver.onError(...) in the catch so a failure does not leave the stream open
Notes the request observer is not thread-safe and must be driven from one thread
anti_behavior: Declares the wrapper method suspend or returns CompletionStage as the Kora contract
Uses an untimed future.get() or latch.await()
Omits onCompleted() or the error path on the request observer
Completes the future in onNext for a bidirectional stream

evals.query: My Kora 2.0 app fails to build with 'Required dependency not found: UserServiceGrpc.UserServiceBlockingStub'. How do I fix it?
expected_behavior: Confirms the @KoraApp interface extends io.koraframework.grpc.client.GrpcClientModule
Confirms io.koraframework:annotation-processors (or symbol-processors for Kotlin) is on the classpath, since it carries the extension that generates the stub factory
Confirms protobuf generation ran and build/generated/source/proto/main/{grpc,java} are on sourceSets.main.java
Checks that no @Tag was placed on the stub parameter, since the extension only serves untagged stub requests
Suggests ./gradlew classes (or generateProto) so generation runs before compilation
Mentions that the enclosing *Grpc class must carry io.grpc.stub.annotations.GrpcGenerated, which comes from protoc-gen-grpc-java
anti_behavior: Suggests adding @Tag to the stub injection as the fix
Suggests writing a manual @Module factory method returning the stub as the primary fix
Blames the BOM version
Suggests editing files under build/generated

evals.query: After renaming packages to io.koraframework, my gRPC client module fails with hundreds of 'package ru.tinkoff.kora.common.annotation does not exist' errors in files I never wrote — all under build/generated/source/proto.
expected_behavior: Identifies stale protobuf generator output: generateProto does not delete its previous output and the build cache key does not account for the package change
Prescribes ./gradlew clean --continue followed by ./gradlew classes testClasses --no-build-cache
States explicitly that generated code must not be hand-edited
Notes the same class of failure applies to any code generator in the module (OpenAPI, wsdl2java)
anti_behavior: Suggests editing the generated sources
Suggests adding ru.tinkoff.kora dependencies back to make it compile
Blames the Kora extension or the BOM

evals.query: I need a 16 MiB max inbound message size and a custom user agent on one Kora 2.0 gRPC client. Which config keys do I set?
expected_behavior: States that neither is a grpcClient config key in Kora 2.0
Provides a Configurer<ManagedChannelBuilder<?>> @Component from io.koraframework.common, tagged @Tag(<Service>Grpc.class)
Notes the tagged configurer runs last in ManagedChannelLifecycle.init(), after every config-driven setting
Notes an untagged Configurer<ManagedChannelBuilder<?>> applies to every channel built by the default OkHttp channel factory
Lists the actual GrpcClientConfig key set so the boundary is clear
anti_behavior: Invents grpcClient.<Service>.maxInboundMessageSize or userAgent keys
Claims the setting is unavailable in Kora 2.0
Suggests replacing GrpcClientModule or building the channel entirely by hand as the first option

evals.query: I bumped protoc to 4.36.2 in my Kora 2.0 gRPC client build to match Kora's own version catalog, and now compilation fails with 'cannot find symbol: class Generated / location: package com.google.protobuf'. The gRPC versions are untouched at 1.84.0.
expected_behavior: Identifies that protoc 4.x generated code references com.google.protobuf.Generated, which does not exist in the protobuf-java the build actually resolves
States that io.grpc:grpc-protobuf:1.84.0 declares protobuf-java 3.25.9 transitively, so the runtime is still on the 3.25 line

Offers the two correct recipes: revert to protoc 3.25.3 (matches the transitive runtime, needs no override), or keep 4.36.2 AND add implementation com.google.protobuf:protobuf-java:4.36.2 so it outranks 3.25.9
Notes that protoc and protobuf-java must move together — bumping one alone is the bug
Notes that kora-bom does not manage protobuf versions
anti_behavior: Suggests adding javax.annotation-api, which supplies javax.annotation.Generated rather than com.google.protobuf.Generated
Blames the Kora annotation processor, KSP, or the generated ApplicationGraph
Recommends excluding protobuf-java or downgrading grpc-protobuf
Suggests a clean build as the fix without changing any version

evals.query: My Kora 2.0 gRPC client adds an x-api-key metadata header in a ClientInterceptor. With grpcClient.PaymentService.telemetry.logging.enabled = true and the request logger at DEBUG the key is printed. How do I mask it, and can I show only the last 4 characters?
expected_behavior: Sets grpcClient.PaymentService.telemetry.logging.maskHeaders = ["authorization", "cookie", "set-cookie", "x-api-key"], explaining that the list replaces the default

Provides a @Tag(GrpcClientTelemetry.class) MaskingStrategy component returning new MaskingKeepLast("***", 4) to keep the last four characters, noting it replaces the default *** strategy for all gRPC clients
States that metadata is logged only at DEBUG on the <full proto service name>.request logger and that the client logs no message bodies
States that there is no mask config key
anti_behavior: Invents a per-client strategy key or a mask config key
Claims header names must be listed in upper case or exactly as the interceptor spelled them
Suggests removing the header in the interceptor to keep it out of the logs
